questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university of Leiden is famous in Indo-European comparative linguistics for their excellent researchers and their novel ideas about the Indo-European proto-languages. Furthermore, many acquaintances are studying or have studied at this university. I had also previously visited the university for summer school in 2021 and was impressed by the wide array of linguistic topics they offered.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. They have an in-depth website, where most questions are answered about arrival, housing, exams, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from the international coordinator for signing my learning agreement in time according to the deadline laid out by the university of Copenhagen. She also helped me greatly in making sure that I was enrolled in the courses I needed, as this had been delayed. The OWL (Orientation Week Leiden) was helpful in helping me getting around the city, getting somewhat acquainted with relevant studen bodies and feeling welcome overall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been excellent to me if the OWL had been organized so that students that shared subjects would be in the same group. But I can fully undestand that not everyone would feel the same way. And it was indeed great to get to know some people very different from myself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was on the waiting list for DUWO housing, but also had a deal with a friend's friend about possible staying in his place while he was abroad. I will recommend to look for other students you know who have either studied in the town or know someone who did. And it can pay off to stay on the waiting list, even if the deposit for housing cannot then be regained.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be much easier than expected. Most time is spent on campus anyway, and travel time is rarely high in the densely populated area around Leiden-Hague-Amsterdam where most students live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing was excellent.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I had great nervousness whether my chosen courses would be accepted, but it was not problem at all. As long as one has read the rules and understand what one is going into, problems are minimal. And they can often be solved by contacting the international coordinator.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international coordinator was very kind in helping me, by phone as well as by e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. But I had not realized before registering that there might be other courses available not in the e-prospectus for the previous year. This is difficult to find out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Decide what kind of courses you want, and perhaps be a bit sceptical about the e-prospectus for last year if the one for the current year is not there yet. Ask the coordinator so that they can ask the professors which courses might become available that are not the old e-prospectus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Excellent material, educators, and library.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All were level 500

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was rather similar. The educators were somewhat more formal, and the classes were larger, so one did not get to know the educators as closely as at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Indo-European Morphology (Noun)
Old Church Slavic Language and Culture
Methodology of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics
The Mycenaean World: Language

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will recommend "The Mycenaean World: Language", as a course in Mycenaean is rarely offered even at higher institutions, and the lecturer is an expert in the field. I would also recommend "Advanced Indo-European Morphology (Noun)" for the very thorough overview of Indo-European cases and interesting perspectives on the reconstruction of (Pre-)Indo-European.

questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than I had feared.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There as a student organisation for linguistics students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To go for a walk around the university. The town is lovely, and there are nice parks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To get more acquainted with the libraries around Leiden and the Hague. Books can be delivered very quickly. I also recommend attending talks by other scholars within the field, of which there is at least one a month.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not very hard. People are more formal, but also friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I am not very good at that either, and I didn't get to know them very well. I was also busy, so I am afraid I might have been rude.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not sure. I am not good with people in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They very much pushed for us to excel. In Denmark, things can be more relaxed, for better and for worse.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do not fret whether it will not work out with your courses or housing. It will.
2. The lecturers are kind and are there to teach. They are not judging you as a person.
3. Appreciate the change of surroundings and the different perspectives on your field of study.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The procedure for resits is unclear. It is important to get in contact with the exchange coordinator if you need any.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new perspectives on my field of study, and the ease at getting the necessary literature from their library.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To make sure that all forms and exams were in order. Mid-term exams were also more common, which gave additional pressure in the middle of the term.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
